summary: SSO session cookie path collision causing tenant session mismatches in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:

FinCloud Apps reports intermittent 403s and wrong-tenant sessions after recent IdP metadata rotation. Root cause appears to be SSO session cookie path attributes being set to '/' by the identity-proxy when tenant routing is path-based (example.com/t/<tenant>), which allows cookies from one tenant to be sent for another tenant's request and results in incorrect tenant binding for the session.

Impact:
- Several FinCloud end-users see 403s when performing console actions as their session is resolved to the wrong tenant.
- Leads to confusing UX where users appear logged in but lack expected entitlements.
- Affects production traffic for a single private deployment customer (FinCloud, enterprise financial SaaS).

Environment:
- Private deployment, single hostname behind customer-managed ingress, path-based tenant routing (/t/<tenant_id>/...).
- Redwood Private v2025.12 with identity-proxy v1.7.3 and authenticator v2.1.
- IdP: Azure AD SAML (customer-managed metadata).

Why unique/different from other SSO bugs in the backlog:
- Not an IdP claim mapping or token signature problem; this is a cookie attribute scoping issue caused by the proxy's default cookie path behavior when tenant path prefixing is used.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy Redwood Private with path-based tenant routing behind a shared hostname (example.com/t/tenant-a and example.com/t/tenant-b).
2) Configure Identity Provider (Azure AD SAML) and perform SSO for tenant-a via /t/tenant-a/sso/callback. Cookie 'rw_session' is issued with Path='/' by identity-proxy.
3) Open a new browser tab, navigate to /t/tenant-b/console while still having 'rw_session' cookie from tenant-a present.
4) Observe session resolves to tenant-a artefacts or user becomes unauthorized for tenant-b resources (403) depending on RBAC checks.
expected_behavior: Session cookies must be scoped to the tenant path (Path=/t/<tenant_id>) or use a tenant-specific cookie name so sessions cannot leak across tenant path prefixes. Requests to /t/tenant-b should not send a cookie that binds to tenant-a's session.
actual_behavior: identity-proxy is setting session cookie Path='/' which is sent on all paths under the hostname. When two tenants share a hostname with path prefixing, the browser sends the same cookie to both tenant paths; session resolution can pick the wrong tenant and RBAC checks then return 403 or wrong entitlements are observed.

comments: Support (2026-03-01) - Maya Chen: Customer first reported this after IdP rotation. They attached screenshot showing logged-in UI but missing tenant resources. Asked for HAR and cookie dump.

Customer (2026-03-01) - FinCloud SRE (Jorge Martinez): Provided HAR, confirms rw_session cookie Path is '/'. Provided tenant routing docs for their ingress. Asked if Redwood expects path or subdomain routing.

Support (2026-03-02) - Liam O'Connor: Replicated locally using path-based routing. Identity-proxy default behavior issues cookie with Path='/' when tenant path prefixing present. Creating investigation ticket INT-4120 for infra change.

Engineering (2026-03-02) - Priya Rao: Noted this is a regression after default cookie refactor in identity-proxy v1.7.0; older versions set tenant-scoped cookie name. Suggests a quick fix: tenant-scoped cookie names + explicit Path setting.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: refactor introduced a single cookie name 'rw_session' and defaulted Path='/' to simplify SameSite behavior; breaks path-scoped multi-tenant deployments.
Confirmed by reproducer: identity-proxy sets Set-Cookie header with Path=/ unconditionally when tenant routing is detected as 'path'.

Trace: authenticator resolves session by looking up session_id in central session store which does not contain tenant context; session record includes tenant scoping, but proxy binding happens pre-route so mismatch occurs.
Observed that switching customer ingress to subdomain-based routing (tenant-a.example.com) avoids problem because cookie scope differs per subdomain.
Dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/sso-sessions?orgId=1 (private) - spike in 403s for fincloud tenant between 09:10-09:20 UTC
resolution: Workaround (customer-side): Configure ingress to use tenant subdomains or enable cookie_path_override in identity-proxy config (set to /t/<tenant_id> via templated header) as a short-term mitigation.

Short-term fix (applied): Released identity-proxy v1.7.4 to FinCloud's Private deployment with a config flag 'tenant_cookie_scoping: path' which sets Set-Cookie Path=/t/<tenant_id> for SSO callbacks. Patch deployed to FinCloud on 2026-03-02 18:45 UTC.
Long-term fix: PR #524 will restore tenant-scoped cookie semantics by default and add unit/integration tests for path-based tenant routing. Target release v1.8.2.

Follow-ups: Add automated e2e test for path-scoped tenants, update Private deploy quickstart to highlight cookie scoping choice, and add console alert when identity-proxy detects path-based routing without cookie scoping enabled.
Customer confirmation: FinCloud SRE confirmed reduction of 403s after patch and accepted the workaround. Plan to keep monitoring for 48 hours.
